### Key takeaways
- Evidence is falling behind output: only 2.5% of 11,628 medical LLM studies were randomized, controlled or prospective, per a [September 2026 analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11770).
- The FDA's generative-AI paper is for [discussion only, not guidance](https://www.maynardnexsen.com/publication-fda-releases-discussion-paper-on-generative-ai-enabled-medical-devices-what-manufacturers-and-investors-need-to-know). Comments closed October 19.
- About 28% of surveyed leaders have deployed agentic AI, and 72% say agents are sometimes implemented without IT approval ([Healthcare Dive](https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/ama-releases-governance-framework-for-agentic-ai-in-healthcare/833120/)).

### What's new
- **Aug 18** — The FDA asked for comments on regulating generative-AI devices, covering risk, premarket review and postmarket monitoring ([FDA](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USFDA/bulletins/424f94a)).
- **Sep 10** — A preprint found 62% of LLM randomized trials tested a discontinued model family ([arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11770)).
- **Sep 11** — ARPA-H awarded $62.7M to build an autonomous heart-failure agent, with deployment at Kaiser Permanente and Duke ([Healthcare Dive](https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/arpa-h-to-invest-62m-to-build-agentic-ai-agent-for-heart-care/830166/)).
- **Oct 15** — The AMA published a governance framework for agents that perform clinical tasks. It says evidence, authority, oversight and accountability must stay aligned ([Healthcare Dive](https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/ama-releases-governance-framework-for-agentic-ai-in-healthcare/833120/)).
- **Nov 5** — Mayo Clinic Platform launched an EHR-integrable decision-support chatbot covering 35+ specialties ([Healthcare Dive](https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/mayo-clinic-platform-launches-ai-tool-to-streamline-clinical-decision-makin/873901/)).

### Novel gaps
1. **Trials that hold up when the model changes.** Evidence: 62% of RCTs tested discontinued models ([arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11770)). Study: platform RCT with pre-set model-swap rules; endpoint: diagnostic accuracy. Funder: PCORI, AHRQ.
2. **LMIC trials big enough to show patient outcomes.** Evidence: a Kenyan trial of ~10,000 encounters found no outcome benefit; experts estimate ~139,000 people are needed ([NPR](https://www.kpbs.org/news/health/2026/07/23/this-ai-tool-promises-a-second-pair-of-eyes-to-clinicians-did-patients-benefit)). Study: cluster RCT; endpoint: treatment failure. Funder: Gates Foundation.
3. **Pediatric LLMs tested inside real workflows.** Evidence: none of 40 pediatric studies tested workflow-integrated LLMs ([JAMA Netw Open](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamanetworkopen/fullarticle/2846946)). Study: stepped-wedge trial in children's hospitals; endpoint: note errors. Funder: NICHD.

### Outlook
We dropped agent deployment trials as a gap because ARPA-H's [Advocate program](https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/arpa-h-to-invest-62m-to-build-agentic-ai-agent-for-heart-care/830166/) now funds them; the open questions are evidence that survives model updates, outcome-powered LMIC trials and pediatric evidence.
